newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says knows nothing on missing Israeli airman.
newsitem.headline: Iran says knows nothing on missing Israeli airman.

text.p: Iran has no information on Israeli airman Ron Arad, shot down over south Lebanon in 1986, Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi said.

He told the official Iranian news agency IRNA on Monday that diplomatic efforts by Iran -- an apparent reference to talks earlier this year with a German mediator who secured a prisoner swap between Israel and Hizbollah in Lebanon -- had concerned the fate of four Iranians missing in Lebanon since 1982.
"Our diplomatic talks concerned the fate of the Iranian diplomats who were kidnapped in Beirut and who were said to have been transferred to Israel," Mohammadi said.
He said that whenever Iran raises the issue of the four "Israel raises the issue of Arad of whom Iran knows nothing."
"Of course, we will spare no effort to find out the fate of our diplomats and secure their freedom," he added.
Israel has said it believes Arad is still alive and held in Iran or by pro-Iranian supporters in Lebanon.

The pro-Iranian Hizbollah group in Lebanon said Arad was captured after his plane was shot down but it did not know if he was now alive or dead. Arad's guards left their post for a while and when they returned he had disappeared, Hizbollah says.
Bernd Schmidbauer, the German security official asked by Israel to trace Arad's fate, said in July it seemed clear he was alive in 1990 but his movements after that were unclear.
Iran said in July it had held talks with Schmidbauer.
German media reports said that Germany has sought Iran's help in tracing Arad's whereabouts but had declined to mediate a swap for the four missing Iranians.

The three diplomats and a journalist went missing during Israel's invasion of Lebanon in 1982. Security reports in Lebanon had said they were captured at a Christian militia checkpoint north of Beirut.
